evidence.basis: Model-editorial candidate selection for practical beginner survival use.
limitations: Not native-speaker certification or completed fluent-human review.
Source links attest only the specific forms or usage principles identified per entry; unlinked forms remain editorial candidates.
Reference only; no active course import, ID mapping, answer-choice validation, reading guide or audio change.
evidence.selection: Focused starter set of 40 practical short expressions and 20 reusable everyday words; order is a category index, not a frequency or teaching sequence.

entries.situation: Greet a stranger or service worker in daytime.

ja.note: Japanese is a daytime greeting; use a time-appropriate greeting at other times.

entries.situation: Leaving a friend or familiar person whom you expect to see again.

ja.note: Casual farewell to someone seen regularly; not a formal departure from a stranger.

sourceRefs.scope: Attests the Japanese expression and greeting/thanks/apology/farewell context.

entries.situation: Thank someone for help or service.

ja.text: ありがとうございます
ja.note: Polite Japanese default; not the casual ありがとう.

entries.situation: Tell someone that their message is not understood.
Ask someone to say the same thing again.

ja.text: もう一度お願いします

sourceRefs.scope: Attests もういちど、お願いします; library spelling uses equivalent kanji 一度 and omits punctuation.

entries.situation: Ask for slower speech.

ja.text: もっとゆっくり話してください

sourceRefs.scope: Supports asking for slower speech. Library form is an editorial adaptation, not an exact quotation.

entries.situation: Ask whether a stranger can communicate in English.
Ask for assistance with an immediate problem.

ja.note: Japanese requests practical assistance; for danger use the urgent help entry.

entries.situation: Call out when in danger or immediate distress.

ja.note: Urgent call; direct wording is appropriate to an emergency.

entries.situation: Ask staff or a passerby for a toilet.
Ask for the railway station.

ja.note: Railway station, not a bus stop.

entries.situation: Order drinking water in a cafe.

ja.note: Latvian and Russian use request forms rather than the dictionary headword.

entries.situation: Ask to pay at the end of a meal.

ja.text: お会計をお願いします

entries.situation: Ask the price of an item being indicated.
Check whether card payment is accepted.
Check whether cash payment is accepted.
Ask for a drink without added sugar.

ja.text: 砂糖なしでお願いします
ja.note: A preparation request, not a guarantee of no sugar in the ingredients.

entries.situation: Decline a shopping bag offered by staff.

ja.note: Japanese naturally declines the bag without adding a literal translation of thanks.

entries.situation: Tell food-service staff about a nut allergy.

ja.text: ナッツアレルギーがあります
ja.note: Broad category only; does not establish which individual allergens or cross-contact risks are covered.

entries.situation: Tell someone you feel physically ill.
Asking someone to summon a doctor when medical help is needed.

ja.text: 医者を呼んでください

entries.situation: Ask another person to summon an ambulance.

ja.text: 救急車を呼んでください

entries.situation: Ask another person to summon police.

ja.text: 警察を呼んでください

entries.situation: Urgently ask someone to stop their current action.

ja.note: Stop an action, not directions for a vehicle to stop or a traffic sign.

entries.situation: Ask someone to stop bothering or approaching you.

ja.note: Firm boundary; Japanese literally asks to be left alone and is context dependent.

entries.situation: Ask for orientation when you cannot find your way.

ja.note: Route-finding only, not a lost possession.

entries.situation: Give a walking direction at a turn.

ja.text: 左に曲がってください

entries.situation: Give a walking direction at a turn.

ja.text: 右に曲がってください

entries.situation: Give a walking direction without turning.

ja.text: まっすぐ行ってください

entries.situation: Pointing out where to stop or receive a service; the action is already understood.

ja.note: Selects the location for an understood action or service. Asking someone to place an object here ordinarily needs ここに rather than ここで.

entries.situation: Indicate the desired place or destination farther away.

ja.note: Point out the location; Japanese そこ usually indicates a place near the listener or already identified.

entries.situation: Ask someone to wait briefly.
Answer a simple positive question affirmatively.

ja.note: For negative questions, languages differ: do not teach automatic word-for-word yes/no equivalence.

entries.situation: Answer a simple positive question negatively.

ja.note: For negative questions, languages differ; a polite refusal may use another expression.

entries.situation: Say that you lack the requested information.

ja.note: Japanese わかりません also covers not understanding; this is a separate communicative meaning, not a distinct distractor.

entries.situation: Ask someone to write information instead of only speaking.
Ask someone to show the thing being discussed.
Politely decline an offer.

ja.note: A polite refusal in response to an offer. Bare 結構です can also express acceptance; keep the refusal context and initial いいえ.
